The CF/PA66 pellets were fed to this single-screw extruder with five heating zones set at different temperatures (2500 C, 2650 C, 2800 C, 2800 C for zone 1, 2, 3, and 4, respectively, and a tip temperature of 2850 C. The material is deposited in rectilinear pattern to form square preforms of different sizes i.e., 10” x 10” and 18” x 18”. The 10” x 10” and 18” x 18” preforms were subsequently machined to the mold sizes of 6” x 6” and 14” x 14”, respectively (refer Fig. 3.2). The machined CF/PA66 preforms of different sizes depicted in Fig. 3.1(a) would fit into the mold for compression overmolding on top of metal inserts as described in Section 3.3. Next, the 20% wt. CF/ABS SFT pellets were used as feedstock material to produce AM preforms. The feedstock material is processed through a single-screw extruder mounted on the KUKA robotic arm that is fitted with a 0.3” diameter nozzle (refer Fig. 3.1(b)). The temperatures of three different zones within the extruder are set as 1900 C, 2300 C, 2500 C for zone 1, 2, and 3, respectively, and a nozzle temperature of 2500 C. The material is deposited in rectilinear pattern into a 14” x 14” mold directly and subsequently compression molded to obtain square plaques of 14” x 14”. The CF/ABS preforms shown in Fig. 3.1(b) would directly fit into the mold for compression overmolding on top of the metal inserts without any additional machining (refer Section 3.3). The mechanical properties of the SFT CF/ABS and LFT CF/PA66 were investigated through tensile testing. The resulting stress-strain characteristic plots were summarized in Section 5.1. The metal inserts of complex geometries suitable for polymer composite overmolding can be manufactured through various AM processes such as Laser Powder Bed Fusion (LPBF) and Binder Jetting. First, triangular lattice mesh with a side length of 11.5 mm, strut thickness of 0.5 mm, and an out of plane thickness of 4 mm and 12 mm were fabricated using grade 300 maraging steel on an AddUp FormUp350 laser powder bed system. Laser Powder Bed Fusion (LPBF) process was chosen to begin with for metal-polymer composite manufacturing as LPBF offers better precision in fabricating thin struts.
